portal_description:
The libguestfs packages contain a library, which is used for accessing and modifying virtual machine (VM) disk images.

This update fixes the following bugs:

* The virt-v2v tool previously failed to download images for conversion from VMware ESX and vCenter hosts. This update prevents unintended rewrites of the download path, which allows the virt-v2v download and conversion to proceed as expected on the mentioned hosts. (BZ#1256823)

* When using the virt-sysprep utility to create a Red Hat Enterprise Linux guest template, the "at" program in the resulting guest could not be used. This update ensures that virt-sysprep does not delete /var/spool/at/.SEQ files in these guests, and "at" now works as expected. (BZ#1238579)

* Previously, it was impossible to boot the virt-p2v ISO image on hardware that used the firmware for Broadcome 10GbE cards and certain other devices. The missing firmware packages have been added to the virt-p2v image, and it can now properly be booted on any hardware supported by Red Hat Enterpise Linux 7. (BZ#983878)

* When using the virt-v2v tool to convert guest images in the qcow2 format into Red Hat Enterprise Virtualization images, the Red Hat Enterprise Virtualization Manager GUI incorrectly displayed the guest's OS type as "Other OS". This problem has been fixed, and the OS type is now displayed correctly. (BZ#1219857)

In addition, this update adds the following enhancements:

* The libguestfs-winsupport subpackage can now be used for performing virtual-to-virtual (virt-v2v) and physical-to-virtual (virt-p2v) conversions of Windows guests. However, with several exceptions such as virt-win-reg, it is no longer possible to use most libguestfs tools on Windows disk images. (BZ#1240276, BZ#1243493)

* KVM now supports virt-v2v conversions of UEFI firmware. As a result, the virt-v2v tool can be used to convert VMware guests with UEFI firmware to KVM guests. (BZ#1184690)

Users of libguestfs are advised to upgrade to these updated packages, which fix these bugs and add these enhancements.
